chief_complaint: sudden choking and coughing fit while eating peanuts followed by persistent unilateral wheezing and unequal breath sounds
hpi_details: 3-year-old boy presenting after choking episode with decreased breath sounds over right hemithorax where inspiratory and expiratory chest radiographs reveal air trapping and hyperinflation of the right lung due to peanut obstruction requiring urgent rigid bronchoscopy.
ideas: He thinks a piece of the peanut went down the wrong pipe and got lodged in his breathing tube.
concerns: He is worried his son's airway will swell shut and he will suffocate in his sleep.
expectations: He hopes the doctor can look inside his throat and safely remove the piece of peanut today.

available_results.value: Persistent right-lung hyperinflation and air trapping on expiration with leftward mediastinal shift; no radiopaque foreign body

teaching.one_liner: 3-year-old boy with a choking episode while eating peanuts, followed by persistent unilateral wheezing and decreased breath sounds.
red_flags: Blue color, inability to speak or cry, marked work of breathing, or lethargy requires immediate emergency intervention

must_ask.say: Can you describe exactly what happened when he started choking on the peanuts?

must_ask.objective: Ask about the timeline since the choking event
must_ask.say: How long ago did the choking happen, and has the wheezing continued since?
Does the wheezing sound like it's coming from one side more than the other?
Is he working hard to breathe, or coughing persistently?
Given the choking history and one-sided findings, we need an urgent procedure to look into his airway and remove the object.

history.answer: He was eating peanuts about two hours ago when he suddenly choked, coughed violently, and now he keeps making a whistling wheezing noise on his right side.
The coughing started suddenly about two hours ago right after he choked on peanuts.
He was chewing a handful of peanuts, gasped, started gagging, and broke into a severe coughing fit.
No, he is not coughing up any phlegm or mucus.
The coughing and noisy breathing have been constant since the choking happened, regardless of whether he is sitting up or lying down.
He had an intense coughing and choking fit right at the beginning, but there is no whooping sound and he has not vomited.
Crying and running around make him breathe faster and cough more, but cold air or dust does not change it.
Yes, I hear a persistent wheezing whistling sound coming specifically from his right chest, and his breathing looks faster than usual.
No, he has not had any fever or chills at all.
No, there has been no blood in his spit or cough.
No, he has been growing well and does not have night sweats or weight loss.
He points to his chest when he coughs as if it feels uncomfortable, but he is only three so he cannot explain it clearly.
No, he has no runny nose, nasal congestion, or mucus dripping down the back of his throat.
No, he does not spit up sour stomach fluid or have reflux symptoms.
No, his breathing is the same whether he is lying flat or upright, and his feet and legs are not swollen.
No, he has never taken any blood pressure or heart medications.
No, nobody smokes in our home or anywhere around him.
No, he has never been around anyone with tuberculosis.
No one at home or in his daycare has had a cough, cold, or any illness recently.
We do not have any pets, mold, or chemical fumes in our home.
He has never had asthma, eczema, or allergic rhinitis.
Yes, I was sitting right next to him and saw him choke on a whole peanut.
His lips and face have not turned blue, and he can still talk and cry, but he seems to be breathing harder.
I think a piece of that peanut went down the wrong pipe and is still stuck in his windpipe.
I'm terrified that his airway will completely close up tonight and he will stop breathing.
I'm hoping you can look inside his throat and get that piece of nut out so he can breathe easily again.
He has always been completely healthy with no chronic medical issues.
He has never had surgery and has never been admitted to a hospital.
He is not taking any prescription drugs, cough syrups, or dietary supplements.
He has no known allergies to medicines, foods, or anything else.
He was born full-term via normal delivery with no newborn complications.
His growth milestones are completely normal and all of his vaccinations are up to date.
He goes to a local daycare center three mornings a week, and he lives with me and his father.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 96/60 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats/min, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air.
Alert child with mild intercostal retractions and slight tachypnea, without cyanosis or stridor.
Nasal mucosa and oropharynx are clear without visible foreign body, erythema, or postnasal discharge.
No palpable cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Slight decrease in chest expansion on the right side; no chest wall tenderness or crepitus.
Hyperresonance to percussion over the right hemithorax compared with the left.
Decreased breath sounds and persistent unilateral expiratory wheezing over the right hemithorax, with normal vesicular breath sounds on the left.
Tachycardic regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, without murmurs or rubs.
No digital clubbing or peripheral edema; capillary refill time is less than two seconds.
